=== page 2 ===
...Scaling this up in accordance with the projected estimates of about 1 000 000 EVs on the road by 2030, the amount of cobalt required for reaching this target number with each of these cathode classes was determined. The calculations indicate that in such a scenario if the current mainstream, NMC 111 (33.3% Co), was the cathode of choice, then the total amount of cobalt required would be ≈2500 tons. Even the next-generation cathodes, such as NMC 811 and NCA which are poised for a broadband commercial deployment in the coming years, would still require ≈700 tons of cobalt to realize this scenario. These numbers though disturbing are still only a conservative estimate because global EV projections for the next half-century are constantly increasing at a burgeoning rate. Our approach, on the other hand, replaces the expensive cobalt with low cost iron and aluminum thus providing a viable solution to this cobalt conundrum. In this scenario, if the NFA cathodes are deployed for the same number of EVs with the same range and pack energies, no cobalt would be required.
